 This is to inform you that the 32
nd AGM of Welspun Enterprises Limite d (the Company) for the financial 
year (FY) 2025-26 is scheduled to be held on Thrusday, August 20, 2026,  at 11:00 a.m. (IST)  through 
Video Conferencing (VC) / Other Audio-Visual Me ans (OAVM) in compliance with the applicable 
Circulars issued by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) and Securities and Exchange Board of 
India (SEBI), and that the deemed venue of the AGM shall be the Registered Office of the Company. 
 
Pursuant to the Regulation 34(1) of SEBI (Lis ting Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) 
Regulations, 2015, (Listing Regulations), please find  enclosed herewith the Notice convening the 32nd 
AGM and the Annual Report of the Company for the FY 2025-26. 
 
In terms of Regulation 46 of the Listing Regulations, the said Notice along with the Annual Report is also available on the website of the Company and can be accessed at www.welspunenterprises.com  and 
on the website of National Securities Depository Limited (NSDL) at https://www.evoting.nsdl.com/   
 
In terms of Section 108 of the Companies Act, 2013, read with Rule 20 of the Companies (Management 
and Administration) Rules, 2014, as amended a nd Regulation 44 of the Listing Regulations, the 
Company is providing facility to its Members to exercise their right to vote by electronic means, through 
remote e-Voting services of NSDL as well as e- Voting during the AGM. The e-Voting instructions and 
the process to join meeting through VC/OAVM is set out in the AGM Notice.  
In accordance with the applicable circulars issued by MCA and SEBI, the Notice of the AGM and the 
Annual Report of the Company for the FY 2025-26, is being sent through electronic mode only to those 
members whose e-mail addresses are registered with  the Company or the Registrar and Share Transfer 
Agent or the Depository Participant(s).

How do I vote electronically using NSDL e-Voting system?
The way to vote electronically on NSDL e-Voting system consists of “Two Steps” which are mentioned below:
Step 1: Access to NSDL e-Voting system
A)  Login method for e-Voting and joining virtual meeting for Individual shareholders holding securities 
in demat mode
  In terms of SEBI circular dated December 09, 2020 on e-Voting facility provided by Listed Companies, Individual 
shareholders holding securities in demat mode are allowed to vote through their demat account maintained with 
Depositories and Depository Participants. Shareholders are advised to update their mobile number and email Id in 
their demat accounts in order to access e-Voting facility.
 Login method for Individual shareholders holding securities in demat mode is given below:-
Type of shareholders Login Method
Individual Shareholders 
holding securities in demat 
mode with NSDL1.  For OTP based login you can click on https://eservices.nsdl.com/SecureWeb/
evoting/evotinglogin.jsp. You will have to enter your 8-digit DP ID, 8-digit Client ID, 
PAN No., Verification Code and generate OTP. Enter the OTP received on registered 
email id/mobile number and click on login. After successful authentication, you 
will be redirected to NSDL Depository site wherein you can see e-Voting page. 
Click on company name or e-Voting service provider i.e. NSDL and you will be 
redirected to e-Voting website of NSDL for casting your vote during the remote 
e-Voting period or joining virtual meeting & voting during the meeting.
2.  Existing IDeAS user can visit the e-Services website of NSDL viz. https://eservices.

EXPLANATORY STATEMENT AS REQUIRED UNDER SECTION 102 OF THE ACT
Item No.3: To appoint a director in place of Mr. Rajesh Mandawewala (DIN: 00007179), who retires by 
rotation, and being eligible, offers himself for re-appointment
Mr. Rajesh R. Mandawewala is the Executive Vice Chairman of Welspun World and one of its founding promoters since 
inception. A pivotal force behind Welspun’s international expansion, Mr. Mandawewala has steered the organization’s 
presence in international markets. His leadership has been instrumental in building scale, operational excellence, and a 
strong customer-centric culture that has defined Welspun’s global reputation.
A Chartered Accountant by qualification, he brings over 35 years of diverse industry experience spanning textiles and 
large-scale manufacturing, including SAW pipes. He is a firm advocate of continuous innovation, research, and product 
development, with a sharp focus on anticipating evolving customer needs and future market trends.
He is a prolific speaker and is associated with leading the business councils such as Confederation of Indian Industry 
(CII), Federation of Indian Chamber of Commerce and Industry (FICCI), Indian Merchants Chamber (IMC), TEXPROCIL 
and Federation of Indian Export Organisations (FIEO) to name a few.
Mr. Mandawewala’ s approach combines financial prudence with operational depth, enabling the Company to consistently 
deliver value through quality, innovation, and competitiveness.

Item No. 7: Approval for Private Placement of 
securities upto ₹1,000 Crore
In terms of Section 42 of the Companies Act, 2013 read 
with Rule 14 of the Companies (Prospectus and Allotment 
of Securities) Rules, 2014 (“the Rules”), a Company shall 
not make Private Placement of its Securities unless the 
proposed offer of Securities or invitation to subscribe to 
Securities has been previously approved by the members 
of the Company by a Special Resolution. The Company 
seeks to pass an enabling resolution to borrow funds from 
time to time in case of an offer or invitation for offer of 
Non - Convertible Debentures (NCDs) and/or Commercial 
Papers (CPs). The Company can pass a Special Resolution 
once in a year for all the offers or invitations to be made for 
such NCDs / CPs during the year. It is proposed to borrow 
funds, by way of issue of securities viz. NCDs / Commercial 
Paper of an amount upto ₹1,000 Crore (Rupees One 
Thousand Crore Only), to be issued on Private Placement 
basis. The issue of NCDs / CPs should help in achieving 
saving in overall cost of borrowing and economical funding 
in the Company as well as its subsidiaries / joint ventures / 
associate companies. Considering the credit rating of the 
Company, the raising of funds through NCDs / CPs would 
be feasible. The approval of the members is sought for 
borrowing limit (apart from temporary loans obtained from 
the Company’s bankers / lenders in the ordinary course

Item No. 9: Approval for material related party 
transactions
Regulatory Requirements for Material Related Party 
Transactions
The Company undertakes infrastructure projects either 
directly or through Special Purpose Vehicles (“SPVs”), 
depending upon the requirements of the relevant 
project structure, concession arrangements with the 
client(s), financing requirements and other commercial 
considerations. Such SPVs may qualify as related 
party(ies) under the Companies Act, 2013 (“Act”) and/or 
the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) 
Regulations, 2015 (“Listing Regulations”). Accordingly, the 
Company may enter into Engineering, Procurement and 
Construction (“EPC”) Contract and other project-related 
arrangements with such SPVs in the ordinary course of 
business for implementation, execution, operation and 
maintenance of infrastructure projects.
Section 188 of the Act read with the applicable Rules 
exempts transactions entered into in the ordinary course of 
business and on an arm’s length basis from the requirement 
of shareholder approval. However, Regulation 23 and 
Schedule XII of the Listing Regulations requires prior 
approval of shareholders by way of an Ordinary Resolution 
for all material related party transactions, irrespective of 
whether such transactions are entered into in the ordinary 
course of business and on an arm’s length basis, unless 
specifically exempted under the Listing Regulations.
Further, SEBI vide Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-
2/P/CIR/2025/18 dated February 14, 2025, Circular 
No. SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-2/P/CIR/2025/93 dated 
June 26, 2025 and Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-
2/P/CIR/2025/135 dated October 13, 2025 (collectively 
referred to as the “SEBI Circulars”) has mandated disclosure 
of minimum information in the format prescribed under the 
Industry Standards while seeking approval of shareholders 
for material related party transactions. Accordingly, the 
prescribed disclosures relating to the proposed transaction 
is provided in Annexure I forming part of this Notice.
Accordingly, the proposed material related party 
transaction between the Company and Welspun Pune 
Shirur Projects Limited (“WPSPL”) is being placed before 
the members for their approval.

Governance Framework
The Company has established a comprehensive Related 
Party Transaction Policy and governance framework 
for review, approval and monitoring of related party 
transactions.
All related party transactions are reviewed by the 
management and placed before the Audit Committee 
together with relevant information, including the business 
rationale, commercial terms, pricing methodology, arm’s 
length justification and overall benefit of the transaction 
to the Company and its shareholders.
The Audit Committee comprises Independent Directors 
and reviews all proposed related party transactions in 
accordance with the provisions of the Act, the Listing 
Regulations, the Company’s Related Party Transaction 
Policy and applicable Industry Standards.
Material related party transactions are placed before the 
Members for prior approval in accordance with Regulation 
23 of the Listing Regulations.
Background, Benefits and Justification of the Proposed 
Transaction
The Pune-Shirur Project has been awarded to Welspun 
Enterprises Limited (“WEL”) based on its technical 
expertise, execution capabilities, resources and experience 
in undertaking projects of a similar nature. Subsequently, 
pursuant to the requirements of the project structure, 
concession arrangement with the client, Welspun Pune 
Shirur Projects Limited (“WPSPL”) was incorporated as 
a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) for implementation and 
execution of the Pune-Shirur Project through a dedicated 
entity. Accordingly, a sub-concession agreement has 
been executed among Maharashtra State Infrastructure 
Development Corporation Limited (“MSIDC”), Government 
of Maharashtra (“GOM”), and WPSPL.
In connection with implementation of the Pune-Shirur 
Project, WPSPL proposes to enter into an Engineering, 
Procurement and Construction (“EPC”) Contract with WEL 
for execution of the Project.
The proposed EPC Contract and other project-related 
transactions and arrangements, in connection with the 
implementation, execution, operation, maintenance 
and administration of the Project, will enable WPSPL to 
leverage WEL’s established execution capabilities, project 
management and technical expertise, resulting in efficient 
execution, ensure better integration of project activities, 
optimise deployment of resources and improved project 
oversight and coordination. Further, considering the long 
execution period of the Pune-Shirur Project, additional 
project-related arrangements, including operation, 
maintenance and other ancillary activities, maybe 
required during the lifecycle of the Project, for which 
WEL and WPSPL may be required to enter into multiple 
project-related transactions from time to time.The proposed transaction is expected to provide long-term 
commercial benefits to WEL by enabling effective 
participation in the execution of the Project, strengthening 
the Company’s order book and creating value for its 
stakeholders. The proposed transaction framework is in 
the ordinary course of business and is aligned with the 
operational and commercial objectives of the Company.
The EPC Contract value of ₹5,420 Crore has been 
determined based on a detailed project cost estimate 
covering materials, labour, plant and machinery, overheads 
and contingencies, together with an appropriate 
methodology adopted for arms’ length pricing in line with 
the prevailing market practices. 
Accordingly, in order to facilitate efficient implementation 
and execution of the Pune-Shirur Project and ensure 
compliance with Regulation 23 of the Listing Regulations, 
approval of the Members of the Company is being sought 
for the proposed transaction, within the limits specified in 
Annexure I forming part of this Notice.
Audit Committee and Board Review
The management had provided the Audit Committee 
and the Board with all relevant information relating to the 
proposed material related party transaction, including 
the rationale, material terms, pricing methodology, 
arm’s length justification and the manner in which the 
proposed transaction is in the interest of the Company. 
The information prescribed under the Industry Standards, 
as set out in Annexure I to this Notice, was also placed in 
the meeting for their consideration.
The Audit Committee and the Board reviewed the 
proposed transaction, including the business rationale, 
commercial terms, pricing methodology, arm’s length basis 
and disclosures prescribed under the Industry Standards. 
They also noted the certificate of the Managing Director 
and Chief Financial Officer confirming that the proposed 
transaction is in the overall interest of the Company, 
and recommends the proposed material related party 
transactions for approval of the Members of the Company 
by way of an Ordinary Resolution.
None of the Directors, Key Managerial Personnel of

passing of Ordinary Resolution set out at Item No. 9 of

Item No. 10: Re-designation and Re-appointment 
of Mr. Balkrishan Goenka (DIN: 00270175) as 
Non-Executive Director, designated as Chairman, 
and approval of remuneration payable
The Members of the Company at the 31st Annual General 
Meeting held on August 29, 2025 had approved the 
re-appointment of Mr. Balkrishan Goenka (DIN: 00270175) 
as Whole-time Director designated as Chairman (Executive) 
for a period of one year with effect from June 01, 2025. 
Accordingly, his present tenure as Executive Chairman 
expired on May 31, 2026.
Based on the recommendation of the Nomination and 
Remuneration Committee (“NRC”), the Board of Directors, 
at its meeting held on May 14, 2026, reviewed the 
leadership and governance structure of the Company 
and approved the transition of Mr. Goenka from Chairman 
(Executive) to Chairman (Non-Executive), with effect from 
June 01, 2026, subject to the approval of the Members of 
the Company.
Mr. Goenka is one of the promoter’s and Chairman of the 
Company from its inception and is a prime architect of 
Welspun World. He is regarded as one of the foremost 
corporate leaders of India. He has over three decades 
of experience in building and leading diversified 
businesses. He has played a pivotal role in the growth 
and transformation of the Welspun Group and continues 
to provide strategic direction and governance oversight 
to the Group. Along with presiding over as the President 
of ASSOCHAM (2019), he has also been the recipient of 
Asian Business Leadership (ABLF) Award, 2019. His deep 
sectoral knowledge, global relationships, and visionary 
leadership have played a pivotal role in steering Welspun 
Enterprises’ transformation into a competitive and 
diversified enterprise.The Board noted that, under Mr. Goenka’s leadership, 
the Company has evolved into a professionally managed 
organization with a strong leadership team, established 
execution capabilities, and a diversified infrastructure 
portfolio. During FY 2025-26, the Company delivered 
strong operational and financial performance and further 
strengthened its growth platform with a consolidated 
order book of approximately ₹20,000 Crore. In view of the 
maturity of the Company’s management structure, it was 
considered appropriate that Mr. Goenka’s role be focused 
on providing strategic direction at the Board level, guiding 
the long-term vision of the Company and strengthening 
governance oversight, while management and execution 
responsibilities continue to rest with the Managing Director 
and the senior management team.
As Chairman (Non-Executive), Mr. Goenka will provide 
leadership to the Board, oversee governance processes, 
facilitate the effective functioning of the Board and its 
Committees and provide guidance on the Company’s 
long-term strategy, growth initiatives and stakeholder 
relationships.
Accordingly, subject to approval of the Members of the 
Company, it is proposed to re-designate and re-appoint 
Mr. Goenka as a Non-Executive Director, designated as 
Chairman of the Company, with effect from June 01, 2026, 
liable to retire by rotation.
Proposed Remuneration
The proposed remuneration comprises only of commission 
linked to the Company’s profitability. No sitting fees, fixed 
remuneration or employee benefits will be payable to 
Mr. Goenka in his capacity as Non-Executive Chairman. 
Accordingly, the remuneration structure aligns his

Under the proposed remuneration structure, Mr. Goenka will transition from an Executive Chairman to a Non-Executive 
Chairman and will no longer receive any fixed remuneration. Instead, he will be eligible to receive only a commission of

For illustration, had the proposed remuneration structure been applicable for FY 2025–26, the remuneration payable at 
3% of the Company’s profit before tax, would have been ~₹17.83 Crore, compared with the aggregate remuneration of 
₹19.38 Crore under the erstwhile remuneration structure (comprising fixed remuneration of ₹7.50 Crore and commission 
of ₹11.81 Crore, computed on the same basis). Accordingly, the proposed remuneration structure would have resulted 
in a lower overall remuneration outflow to the Company while aligning the Chairman’s remuneration entirely with the 
Company’s financial performance.
The proposed remuneration is within the limits prescribed under Section 197 of the Companies Act, 2013 and shall be 
subject to the applicable provisions of Schedule V thereto in the event of absence or inadequacy of profits.

Mr. Garg is a distinguished industry leader with over four 
decades of experience across infrastructure, engineering 
and project execution businesses. He holds a Bachelor’s 
degree in Engineering from the University of Roorkee and 
is an alumnus of the Harvard Business School’s Advanced 
Management Program. Prior to joining the Welspun

overseas and led businesses involved in roads, elevated

under the Hybrid Annuity Model. Under his leadership, 
the Company has built a robust transportation vertical, 
while also exploring opportunities in the tunnelling 
segment. In addition to the transportation business, he 
has spearheaded the development of the water vertical, 
establishing a strong platform with a healthy order book. 
To further strengthen and diversify the Company’s 
portfolio, Mr. Garg led the acquisition of Welspun Michigan 
Engineers Limited, thereby expanding the Company’s 
capabilities in advanced trenchless technologies. 
Additionally, the Company has broadened its presence 
in technology-driven water treatment solutions through 
SmartOps. His leadership has been instrumental in the 
successful execution and delivery of several landmark 
projects.
Under Mr. Garg’s leadership, the Company continued 
to deliver strong operational and financial performance 
during FY2025–26, despite industry-wide challenges.

Dear Members,
The Securities and Exchange Board of India, vide its 
latest Master Circular No. SEBI/HO/MIRSD/POD-1/P/ 
CIR/2024/37 dated 7th May 2024, has issued guidelines 
on common and simplified norms for processing investor’s 
service requests by RTAs, has notified common and 
simplified norms for processing investor’s service request 
by the Registrars and Transfer Agents (RTAs) and norms 
for furnishing Permanent Account Number (“PAN”), Know 
Your Client (“KYC”) details and Nomination.
In terms of the aforesaid circular, all holders of physical 
securities of the Company are mandatorily required to 
furnish the following documents / details to the Company’s 
RTA i.e. MUFG Intime India Private Limited (Formerly known 
as Link Intime India Private Limited) (“MUFG Intime”) along 
with Form ISR-1 for updating their KYC detail:-
a. PAN
b. Nomination
c. Contact Details
d. Bank Account details
e. Specimen Signature
In case of mismatch in the signature of the holder in the 
records of MUFG Intime, the investor shall furnish original 
cancelled cheque and banker’s attestation of the signature 
as per Form ISR-2.
Investors shall continue to use form SH-13 and SH-14 
for declaration of nomination and change in nomination 
respectively. However, in case investor wants to opt-out 
of nomination, Form ISR-3 shall be filed.
The security holder(s) whose folio(s) do not have PAN, 
Choice of Nomination, Contact Details, Bank Account 
Details and Specimen Signature updated, shall be eligible:
•  to lodge grievance or avail any service request from 
the RTA only after furnishing PAN, KYC details and 
Nomination.GUIDELINES ON COMMON AND SIMPLIFIED NORMS FOR PROCESSING INVESTOR’S SERVICE REQUESTS 
BY REGISTRARS AND TRANSFER AGENTS (RTAS)
•  for any payment including dividend, interest or 
redemption payment in respect of such folios, 
only through electronic mode with effect from 
April 01, 2024. An intimation shall be sent by the 
Listed Company/ Entity to the security holder that 
such payment is due and shall be made electronically 
only upon complying with the requirements stated in 
Para 19.1 of the Master Circular.
In this regard kindly take note of the below
1.  In case of non-updation of (a) PAN or (b) Choice 
of Nomination or (c) Contact Details or (d) Mobile 
Number or (e)Bank Account Details or (f) Specimen 
Signature in respect of physical folios, dividend/ 
interest/redemption payment etc. shall be paid only 
through electronic mode with effect from April 01, 
2024 upon furnishing all the aforesaid details in 
entirety.
2.  If a security holder updates the (a) PAN or (b) Choice 
of Nomination or (c) Contact Details or (d) Mobile 
Number or (e)Bank Account Details or (f) Specimen 
Signature after April 01, 2024, then the security holder 
would receive all the dividends/interest/redemption 
payment etc. declared during that period (from 
April 01, 2024 till date of updation) pertaining to the 
securities held after the said updation automatically.
In this connection you are required to update your folio 
either with (a) PAN or (b) Choice of Nomination or (c) 
Contact Details or (d) Mobile Number or (e)Bank Account 
Details or (f) Specimen Signature or all of the above in 
entirety and furnish the details/documents (Form No. 
ISR-1, ISR-2, ISR-3 & Form No. SH13 / 14) as applicable.
Investors are requested to ensure the above details are 
updated with MUFG Intime at the earliest.

PROGRESS WITH  
PURPOSE
At Welspun Enterprises, we believe infrastructure is more than engineering. It is a 
catalyst for economic growth, social inclusion and environmental resilience. Every 
road we build shortens distances between people and opportunities. Every water 
project improves quality of life and strengthens communities. Every tunnel, bridge and 
infrastructure asset contributes to a stronger, more connected India.
Welspun Enterprises’ journey reflects the evolution of 
India’s infrastructure ambitions. From roads and water 
to wastewater, tunnelling and urban infrastructure, the 
company is building capabilities that go beyond project 
delivery. Its success is measured through the value its 
assets create over time – for communities, businesses, 
governments and future generations.
Progress reflects our commitment to delivering world-class 
infrastructure with excellence, innovation, and reliability. 
Purpose reflects our responsibility to create sustainable 
value, through safer workplaces, responsible resource 
management, environmental stewardship, and meaningful 
community impact.
Our projects are built by people whose expertise, dedication 
and resilience transform plans into reality. From engineers 
and project managers to safety leaders and frontline 
workers, every individual contributes to a larger mission. 
Their stories are as important as the infrastructure they 
help create.We consider ourselves not merely as an EPC company, 
but as a trusted architect of India’s sustainable future. 
A company that combines engineering excellence with 
human impact. A company that creates infrastructure not 
just for today, but for generations to come.
Because infrastructure is not only about what we build.
It is about the progress we enable.
Welspun Enterprises.

Dear Shareholders,
It is my pleasure to present the 32nd Annual Report of Welspun 
Enterprises Ltd (WEL) for FY 2025-26. 
I am happy to share that WEL has remained true to its 
mission i.e., progressive, purpose-led infrastructure 
Company. We continue to build a differentiated infrastructure 
business centred on complex and value-accretive projects. 
The Company’s performance is underpinned by a strong 
people-first culture and I am happy to share that WEL for 
the second time has been certified as a Great Place to Work 
(GPTW), reflecting our employee-led ethos and our core 
values of Learning, Innovation, Trust & Transparency and 
Endurance (LITE).
EXECUTION EXCELLENCE & ORDER BOOK VISIBILITY
FY 2025-26 demonstrated our execution excellence and our 
right to strategic win. The Aunta–Simaria Ganga Bridge Road 
Project in Bihar is India’s widest extradosed bridge over the 
River Ganga, spanning 1.8 km, which was inaugurated by 
the Hon’ble Prime Minister of India. This project is another crown jewel in our portfolio, showcasing our ability to deliver 
complex and world-class infrastructure. 
We secured over ₹10,000 crore in new orders, including 
the Panjrapur Water Treatment Plant and the Pune–Shirur 
six-lane, partially elevated highway corridor on a DBFOT 
toll basis. Our consolidated order book including O&M 
aggregates to approximately ₹ 20,000 crore, ensuring strong 
revenue visibility and a solid foundation for future growth. It 
is a matter of great pride for all stakeholders of the Company 
that upon commissioning of the Panjrapur and Bhandup 
facilities, WEL will manage over 50% of Mumbai’s potable 
water, reinforcing the Company’s position as a leading player 
in urban water infrastructure.
INDUSTRY RECOGNITION REFLECTING OPERATIONAL 
EXCELLENCE
For the financial year, we have received several awards 
and accolades reaffirming the Company’s commitment to 
excellence across its businesses.  “Best Construction Methodology of the Year” by Build 
India Awards  for Aunta Simaria Road Project Bridge over 
Ganga River
 “Most Admired Company – Transportation” by ET Now 
Infra Focus Awards
 “Best Brand in Construction & Infrastructure (Water 
Technology)” – ET Now Infra Focus Awards 
 “Innovative Climate Action Awards” - India Climate 
Samman 2026 by Carbon Markets Association of India
 “Best Tunneller of the Year” - (IndSTT) 
HEALTHY OPERATIONAL PERFORMANCE AND STRONG 
FINANCIAL POSITION
The Company’s financial performance during the year 
reflected the resilience of the business model. Despite 
extended monsoons and time intensive project approval 
cycles, the Company delivered a healthy operational 
performance, with consolidated EBITDA increasing 16% 
year-on-year to ₹845 crore, driven by strong execution 
across business verticals and continued focus on operational 
efficiency and cost optimisation.
The Company maintained a robust balance sheet with 
consolidated cash and cash equivalents of approximately 
₹1,700 crore. During the year, we completed ₹1,000 crore 
preferential issuance, receiving ₹250 crore as allotment 
money, with the balance expected within 18 months of 
allotment. This further strengthens our financial position to 
pursue growth opportunities while maintaining disciplined 
capital allocation. Reflecting our financial strength, CRISIL 
upgraded our outlook from Stable to Positive, while 
reaffirming our AA- long-term and A1+ short-term ratings.
CREATING SHAREHOLDER VALUE & PARTNERING IN 
INDIA’S PROGRESS
For the year, the Board has recommended a dividend of  
₹3 per share, underscoring commitment to sustainable value 
creation and consistent returns for shareholders.
Looking ahead, I am confident of the opportunities unfolding 
across three strategic infrastructure themes – water security, 
underground infrastructure, and transportation connectivity.
Water security remains one of India’s most critical priorities. 
According to NITI Aayog, the Country’s water demand is 
expected to outpace available supply by 2030, underscoring 
the need for sustained investments across entire water 
ecosystem. This offers an opportunity to build resilient and 
sustainable infrastructure that supports India’s long-term 
growth.
WEL is well poised to contribute towards this multi-decade 
transformation, backed by a strong execution track record 
and differentiated capabilities. Our landmark projects 
under construction – including India’s first multi-storeyed, 
low-footprint wastewater treatment plant at Dharavi and 
the 2,000 MLD Bhandup Water Treatment Facility, Asia’s 
largest single-source water treatment plant – reflect our proven ability to execute complex, engineering-intensive 
projects at scale. This capability is complemented by our 
proprietary, technology-led solutions for the at-source 
restoration and rejuvenation of kunds (ponds) and other 
water bodies, expanding our presence across the water 
value chain and reinforcing our ability to deliver integrated, 
sustainable solutions for India’s evolving water management 
requirements.
Rapid urbanisation and limited land availability are 
simultaneously driving the need for robust underground 
infrastructure. With nearly 3,000 km of tunnels planned 
across India over the next decade, tunnelling is emerging 
as a key enabler of urban mobility and utility infrastructure. 
Building on the specialised water tunnelling expertise of our 
subsidiary, Welspun Michigan Engineers Limited (WMEL), we 
are strategically expanding our capabilities into transport and 
metro tunnelling.
WEL continues to play its part in India’s infrastructure 
growth by developing projects that strengthen connectivity 
and support economic progress. The Pune–Shirur Partially 
Elevated Corridor, being executed under the DBFOT model, 
reflects this commitment. Being an important mobility 
corridor, it will ease congestion, improve regional connectivity 
and enable more efficient movement of people and goods. 
OIL & GAS: UNLOCKING STRATEGIC ENERGY RESOURCES
As India strengthens energy security and reduces import 
dependence, domestic natural gas assumes increasing 
strategic importance. Our joint venture with Adani holds 
three adjacent offshore blocks – Mumbai, B-9 and C37 – with 
an estimated GIIP of 1.1 TCF. Leveraging a cluster-based 
development approach and existing offshore infrastructure, 
we are advancing these assets towards commercial 
development, creating long-term value for both the nation 
and our stakeholders.
SUSTAINABILITY & PEOPLE: BUILDING LONG-TERM 
RESILIENCE
FY 2025-26 marked another step forward in embedding 
sustainability across our business. Enhanced ESG governance 
enabled a 20% reduction in cement consumption through 
alternative materials, supporting our 2040 carbon neutrality 
ambition. Simultaneously, focussed people initiatives 
reduced attrition by 4% and improved workforce diversity 
from 6% to 8%, strengthening organisational resilience.
ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS
I thank all our stakeholders for their continued trust and 
support as we remain committed to creating sustainable, 
long-term value together.
Warm Regards,
B K Goenka
Chairman

It is my privilege to address you as the Lead Independent

FY 2025-26 was a year of strategic progress, disciplined 
execution and continued value creation. Despite an 
extended monsoon, project clearance delays and project 
execution challenges, your Company demonstrated 
resilience by delivering a 16% growth in consolidated 
EBITDA and an 11% growth in consolidated profit after tax, 
reflecting the strength of its diversified business model, 
prudent financial management and execution capabilities.
The Company continued to strengthen its position as one 
of India’s leading integrated infrastructure developers 
across both transportation and water sectors. During the 
year, the Company further expanded its water portfolio 
by securing the prestigious 910 MLD Water Treatment 
Plant at Panjrapur from the Brihanmumbai Municipal 
Corporation. Together with the 2,000 MLD Bhandup 
Water Treatment Plant already under execution, the two Dear Stakeholders,
projects are expected to contribute significantly towards 
Mumbai’s future drinking water infrastructure. Progress also 
continued across key ongoing projects, including the 
Dharavi Wastewater Treatment Plant, Dharavi–Ghatkopar 
Tunnel and the Uttar Pradesh Jal Jeevan Mission projects, 
reinforcing the Company’s growing expertise across the 
entire water infrastructure value chain.
The transportation business also achieved significant 
milestones during the year with the award of the Pune–
Shirur 6-Lane Partially Elevated Corridor Project in 
Maharashtra on a DBFOT basis, valued at approximately 
`7,300 crore, this marquee project further strengthens 
the Company’s transportation portfolio and reinforces 
its capability to execute large, technically complex 
infrastructure projects. During the year, your Company 
also successfully completed the Aunta–Simaria Road 
Project, featuring India’s widest extradosed bridge, which 
was inaugurated by the Hon’ble Prime Minister of India. 
This landmark achievement reflects your Company’s engineering excellence, execution capabilities and 
commitment to nation-building. Your Company continues 
to pursue opportunities selectively across EPC, HAM and 
BOT models while maintaining a disciplined approach 
towards capital allocation and risk management.

the year, providing strategic guidance and oversight

OUR EVOLUTION TOWARDS CORE 
INFRASTRUCTURE STRENGTH
At WEL, we have steadily evolved into a focussed 
player in Transportation infrastructure, Water, and 
Tunnelling. Our focussed evolution reflects a clear 
strategic intent to concentrate on nation’s complex, 
high-impact infrastructure projects that are critical 
to urban development. Over the years, we have 
transitioned towards building deep capabilities in these 
core segments, anchored in our execution excellence 
and engineering expertise.
We have strengthened our position across Roads, 
Highways, Water Supply and Water Treatment by 
selectively pursuing projects that are value-accretive, 
technically complex, and aligned with our ability to 
deliver engineering-led innovation.SERVING SPECIALISED DOMAINS WITH A 
DIFFERENCE

Projects Undertaken
Dharavi Wastewater 
Treatment Facility, Mumbai
The Dharavi Wastewater Treatment Facility marks Welspun 
Enterprises’ most significant water infrastructure project 
in India, reflecting our growing presence in essential 
urban sanitation. The 418-MLD WwTF is being built 
over 12.7-acres of land. The total consideration value 
of `4,436 crore includes operations & maintenance and 
asset replacement. Once commissioned, this will be India’s 
first multi-storey sewage treatment facility.
The development encompasses end-to-end responsibilities, 
including design, construction and 15 years of operations 
and maintenance. This will ensure consistent performance, 
create local employment opportunities, and support 
long-term skill development – advancing water circularity 
and contributing to a cleaner, more sustainable city of 
Mumbai. The project has the lowest footprint/MLD and 
is capable of treating sewage generated by a population 
of nearly 3.5 million people. Around 50% of the treated 
wastewater will be tertiary treated.
Designed with advanced, space-optimised technology, 
the facility adopts a multi-storeyed configuration that 
maximises land-use efficiency. It is India’s first vertical 
wastewater treatment plant and is one of the few 
large-scale facilities of its kind globally. The project 
underscores our commitment to innovation, operational 
excellence and sustainable infrastructure, setting new 
benchmarks in efficiency and environmental performance.CURRENT PROGRESS
The Dharavi Wastewater Treatment Facility has achieved 
approximately 65% overall progress and remains on track 
to be completed by July 2027. Civil works for the SBR 
and blower units have been completed, and mechanical 
erection has commenced. Major equipment deliveries are 
also underway, marking the project’s transition to a critical 
installation phase.KEY HIGHLIGHTS FOR FY 2025-26

=== page 56 ===
The 2,000 MLD Bhandup Water Treatment Plant marks a 
significant milestone in Welspun Enterprises’ commitment to 
delivering water infrastructure designed to support reliable 
treatment capacity and long-term operational efficiency. 
Located within Mumbai’s primary drinking water hub at the 
BMC Bhandup Complex, the project is being executed on a 
design-build basis over 48 months, followed by 15 years of 
operations and maintenance.
In collaboration with Veolia, a global leader in water 
technologies, the project uses advanced treatment solutions 
to improve efficiency, optimise resource use and support 
environmental sustainability. Its technology-led design 
reduces land requirement to approximately 0.003 ha/MLD, 
offering nearly five to six times greater area efficiency than 
a conventional water treatment plant.
CURRENT PROGRESS
The Letter of Award (LOA) was received in February 2024 and 
notice to commence in July 2024. The total consideration 
value of `4,281 crore includes operations & maintenance and asset replacement. Engineering and excavation are 
under progress and construction work has commenced. 
Having received critical statutory clearances, the 
subcontractor was finalised and deployed, and the 
batching plants were set up with mass excavation 
completed up to ~30% for major process structures. 
Construction activities are now progressing across key 
work fronts. These milestones have enabled the project 
to move into active execution. The project is expected to 
be completed by April 2029.

=== page 57 ===
Rural Water Supply Project under 
Jal Jeevan Mission, Uttar Pradesh
The Rural Water Supply Project under Jal Jeevan Mission 
reflects the Company’s focus on inclusive development, 
sustainable infrastructure and community impact.
The project is part of the Government of India’s Har Ghar 
Nal Se Jal programme and involves developing end-to-end 
water supply infrastructure across more than 2,500 villages 
in Uttar Pradesh. It is designed to provide access to clean 
drinking water for nearly 44 lac beneficiaries.
The project includes water supply systems, over 1,000 tube 
wells, solar-powered pump houses, package chlorination 
plants, elevated service reservoirs, 15,000 km of pipelines 
and 6 lac house service connections. In line with the 
Company’s ESG focus, solar panels totalling 27 MW are 
being installed across project sites to offset the grid 
electricity required for pumping operations.CURRENT PROGRESS
The project has achieved 94% pipeline completion, with 
O&M commenced for 84 out of 1,068 schemes and trial 
runs started for 254 villages. Upon completion, the project 
will benefit over 2,500 villages and support long-term 
access to safe drinking water across key regions of Uttar 
Pradesh.

Tertiary Treated Conveyance Tunnel 
Project, Mumbai
The Tertiary Treated Conveyance Tunnel project involves 
the design and construction of an 8.48 km tertiary treated 
water conveyance tunnel from Dharavi WwTF to Ghatkopar 
WwTF. Executed using TBM, the project will support 
Mumbai’s wastewater reuse ecosystem by conveying 
treated water for further refinement and reuse and support 
the circular economy of water.
CURRENT PROGRESS
The Letter of Award was received in October 2024, 
followed by the notice to commence in November 2024. 
The project has a total consideration value of ₹2,163 crore, 
excluding GST.
Project clearances have taken longer than anticipated, 
delaying the main execution phase. Following the receipt 
of pre-project clearances, shaft work for the approximately 
150-metre-deep shaft at Ghatkopar is expected to 
commence shortly.Spanning 93 months for design and build, the project will 
enable the underground transfer of tertiary treated water 
from Dharavi WwTF to Ghatkopar WwTF. In conjunction 
with the Dharavi Wastewater Treatment Facility, the project 
will strengthen Mumbai’s wastewater reuse ecosystem and 
support the Company’s Growth and Green vision.

BorivaliPriority Sewer Tunnel Phase-I (PST-1) Project
The Priority Sewer Tunnel Phase-I Project is designed to 
strengthen Mumbai’s wastewater infrastructure through a deep 
underground sewer network. Engineered to navigate dense 
urban conditions and complex ground strata, the project will 
improve the reliability and operational efficiency of the city’s 
wastewater system while reducing environmental impact.
Project Status:
 During the year, tunnelling work progressed steadily, with 
4,845 m completed out of the total project scope of 5,850 
m as per the reporting cut-off. Segment casting at the 
Nadal casting yard also advanced, with 4,698 segments 
completed out of 4,875
 The tunnel is being constructed using a Rock Slurry Tunnel 
Boring Machine. A 50 m stretch under the New Austrian 
Tunnelling Method has been completed, and concrete 
lining work across all 15 shafts has also been completed
Priority Sewer Tunnel Phase-II (PST-2) Project
The Priority Sewer Tunnel Phase-II Project is designed to 
strengthen Mumbai’s wastewater collection and conveyance 
network under the Mumbai Sewer Disposal Project Stage-II.
Engineered for dense urban conditions, the tunnel alignment 
is being executed using a Rock EPB Tunnel Boring Machine 
capable of navigating mixed and complex ground strata. 
The project will improve the reliability of wastewater collection, 
reduce pressure on existing collector sewers and support more 
efficient sewage conveyance with minimal surface disruption.
Project Status:
 The PST-2 tunnel spans approximately 4.7 km and is being 
constructed using a 2.6 m tunnel diameter Rock EPB Tunnel 
Boring Machine. The TBM is designed to operate across 
varied geological conditions, including silty sand, silty clay, 
boulders, breccia, basalt and clay with gravel
 The project has also achieved a significant tunnelling 
milestone with the successful navigation of an 87  m radius  
curve, demonstrating the ability to execute complex 
underground works in constrained urban environments
 The New Austrian Tunnelling Method has been completed, 
and concrete lining work across all 15 shafts has also 
been completed
Microtunnelling Projects
The project reflects WMEL’s expertise in trenchless pipeline 
installation for dense urban environments. Executed with minimal 
surface disruption, microtunnelling enables underground utility 
development while reducing open excavation, traffic impact 
and disruption to surrounding communities.
 Eastern Express Highway: Microtunnelling project from

 Tata Power: Railway crossing works through microtunnelling

 Micro 1: Microtunnelling project comprising three packages 
at Dahisar, Kandivali and Bandra.
 Micro 5: Microtunnelling project comprising three packages. 
Two packages, at Malad and Charkop, have been completed, 
while work at Vallabh Nagar is in progress.

Haji Ali Stormwater Pumping Station
The Haji Ali Stormwater Pumping Station is an important 
part of Mumbai’s stormwater drainage network. After years 
of operation, the facility is being upgraded to improve 
reliability, extend asset life and strengthen stormwater 
evacuation during heavy rainfall and high-tide conditions.
The scope includes mechanical, electrical, 
instrumentation and automation works, civil repairs, 
and comprehensive operations and maintenance 
for 15 years.
Through this project, WMEL will support Mumbai’s 
flood-mitigation infrastructure and improve drainage 
performance in critical urban catchments.
Vehar Pumping Station
The Vehar Pumping Station is designed to capture 
overflow water from Vehar Lake and transfer it to 
the Bhandup Water Complex for treatment, helping 
reduce monsoon water wastage and improve usable 
freshwater availability.
The project includes the intake channel, intake structure 
and pumping station, along with civil, mechanical, electrical, instrumentation and control works. With a 
planned capacity of 200 MLD, it will support Mumbai’s 
freshwater supply during the monsoon season. It also 
contributes to better water management by reducing 
uncontrolled overflow and supporting the efficient transfer 
of excess lake water for treatment and use.
Construction is progressing at site, with substructure 
works completed and superstructure works underway.
Mogra Stormwater Pumping Station
The Mogra Stormwater Pumping Station is a critical 
flood-mitigation project in Mumbai’s K/W Ward. Planned along 
Mogra Nallah near Oshiwara and Lokhandwala, the project 
is expected to improve stormwater discharge and reduce 
waterlogging in flood-prone areas such as Oshiwara, 
Andheri, Versova and Jogeshwari.
With key coastal approvals progressing, the project 
is moving closer to execution. Once completed, it will 
strengthen Mumbai’s stormwater drainage network and 
support faster evacuation of rainwater during heavy 
monsoon and high-tide conditions.STORMWATER PUMPING STATIONS
Mumbai receives intense rainfall during the monsoon season, with most falling between June and September. As a coastal 
city, its stormwater drainage is also affected by tidal variations, especially when high tide restricts the natural discharge 
of runoff into the sea.
To strengthen flood management and improve stormwater evacuation from low-lying, flood-prone areas, stormwater 
pumping stations with floodgates are proposed at critical locations across the city. These facilities will help regulate 
outflows, reduce backflow during high tide, and support faster stormwater discharge during peak rainfall events. 
Welspun Enterprises manages infrastructure accounting for 50% of Mumbai’s stormwater pumping capacity.

Aunta–Simaria Road Project 
(ASRP), Bihar
Varanasi–Aurangabad Road Project 
(VARP), Uttar Pradesh and Bihar
The Aunta–Simaria Road Project stands out as a strong 
example of Welspun Enterprises’ engineering capability 
in complex transportation infrastructure. Executed for the 
National Highways Authority of India, the 8.15-km project 
includes the widening of a critical section of NH-31 and 
the construction of a 1.8-km extradosed bridge across the 
River Ganga, India’s widest of its kind.
Beyond its scale, the Project is notable for the engineering 
solutions deployed in challenging site conditions. A key 
achievement was the construction of a railway underbridge 
below the Rampur–Dumra railway line, an active rail corridor 
that carries more than 200 trains every week. The work 
was completed within limited railway block windows, 
with minimal disruption to rail movement and in weak, 
waterlogged soil conditions where conventional methods 
were not feasible.
This solution has been featured in Indian Highways , the 
technical journal of the Indian Roads Congress, as an 
important case study in railway underpass construction. 
The team used the Push Box method, casting large RCC 
boxes outside the railway embankment and pushed them 
into position below the tracks. Pile foundations were then 
constructed from the top of the boxes and integrated with 
the structure to support future rail and road loads.
The Project strengthens connectivity between North and 
South Bihar and onward to Northeast India. It reduces travel time between Patna and Begusarai by nearly one hour and 
unlocks access to national and international markets for local 
Makhana farmers and improves connectivity to industrial 
hubs like Barauni, driving regional economic growth.
CURRENT PROGRESS
The Project was inaugurated by the Hon’ble Prime Minister, 
Shri Narendra Modi, in August 2025. The second annuity 
payment from NHAI has been received as scheduled, and 
the Project is on track for monetisation.
Featured in Indian Highways , the 
technical journal of the Indian Roads 
Congress, the Aunta–Simaria Road 
Project presents an important case study 
in railway underpass construction.

OUR ESG PRIORITIES
Shaping ESG-aligned, Sustainable, 
Resilient, and Future-ready Infrastructure
We understand that infrastructure development must not 
only address present-day challenges, it should also pave 
the way for a resilient and sustainable future for generations 
to come. Infrastructure, for us, is not just about building 
assets – it is about engineering long-term value through 
sustainability.
AN UNPRECEDENTED INFRASTRUCTURE  
BUILD-OUT IN INDIA
The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) has 
estimated that nearly 75% of the infrastructure that will exist 
by 2040 globally is yet to be built. This positions emerging 
economies like India at the centre of a once-in-a-generation opportunity to shape sustainable and resilient infrastructure. 
At the same time, the built environment contributes ~37–39% 
of global energy-related CO₂ emissions, with construction 
materials such as cement alone accounting for ~7–8% of 
global emissions (UNEP; IEA, 2024). This underscores the 
dual challenge of scaling infrastructure, while reducing its 
environmental footprint. 
India’s infrastructure sector contributes ~9% to GDP and 
supports over 50 million jobs, making it a critical driver 
of economic growth (IBEF, 2024). The nation stands at 
a defining moment in its development journey with an 
estimated `111 lac crore National Infrastructure Pipeline Engineering Viksit Bharat
At	Welspun	 Enterprises,	 our	approach	 remains	 focussed	 on	structured	 progression	 - 
building	 on	established	 practices,	 improving	 consistency	 across	 projects,	 and	 
embedding	 ESG	more	firmly	into	core	business	 processes	 to	drive	long-term,	 sustainable	
value	creation.with 67 lac km roads to be developed, over 40,000 
MLD additional water treatment capacity required, and 
significant expansion needed in wastewater and tunnelling 
infrastructure. India is currently at a pivotal stage in its 
development journey and is witnessing an unprecedented 
infrastructure build-out.
Nevertheless, this scale of infrastructure also ushers in 
significant systemic challenges. The infrastructure and 
construction sectors contribute ~2.7 billion tCO₂e annually 
(IEA, 2023) and consume approximately 1.6 billion tonnes 
of virgin materials (CII, 2022), highlighting its substantial 
environment footprint. In parallel, construction and 
demolition waste is rising, estimated at 150–500 million 
tonnes annually (CPCB, 2022-23), underscoring increasing 
pressure on resource efficiency. Amid these challenges, water is emerging as a 
critical constraint for infrastructure development. 
Concrete production alone requires 600–700 litres per 
m³ of concrete (ACI, 2019), reflecting high water intensity 
across construction processes. 
SUSTAINABLE & RESILIENT INFRASTRUCTURE  
IN ACTION 
The context calls for a fundamental shift – from a linear 
“take–make–dispose” model to a circular, low-carbon 
infrastructure paradigm (UNEP, 2020). At the same 
time, circular economy approaches in construction have 
the potential to reduce embodied carbon by 40–50%, 
particularly through the use of supplementary cementitious 
materials and recycled inputs (World Economic Forum, 
2023-24).

WEL is institutionalising a structured, risk-based ESG VCP 
framework to extend sustainability across its value chain 
partners and strengthen Scope 3 action. The framework 
follows a step-wise approach – vendor universe 
definition, spend-based prioritisation, ESG assessment, 
scoring, and continuous monitoring – aligned with SEBI 
BRSR requirements. 
At the foundation, all value chain partners are aligned 
to ESG due diligence under the Supplier Code of 
Conduct, ensuring a consistent baseline development 
of responsible practices. 
•  The Company has already considered physical climate 
risk assessments, with focus on across key assets 
to identify exposure to key climate considerations 
into project planning and decision-making hazards. 
This will be further strengthened through the adoption 
of a structured, science-based methodology aligned 
with global frameworks, assessing risk as a function 
of hazard, exposure, and vulnerability. 
•  Expanded scope to cover priority acute and chronic 
hazards such as flooding, extreme precipitation, heat 
stress, and water stress across baseline and future 
climate-related scenarios Category 1 Implementation in Practice – Chevrox Case 
(Bhandup RMC Plant) 
WEL’s engagement with Chevrox demonstrates how 
ESG is translated from framework to on-ground 
implementation at category 3, particularly at critical 
control points.

Case Study 3Welspun Foundation launched its 
flagship programme WelNetrutva 
in Dibai and Danpur blocks of 
Bulandshahr district, in partnership 
with RASTA, a Delhi-based NGO. 
The initiative aimed at empowering 
50 rural women across five villages 
by supporting them in establishing 
50 micro-enterprises. During the 
Programme, anaemia screening of 
2,000 women revealed alarming 
results – the women faced poor 
menstrual hygiene practices, and did 
not have any access to affordable 
sanitary pads. 
Hajra, one of the participants, stood 
up with her daughter Mehvish with 
a clear and courageous vision – to 
start a sanitary pad enterprise and 
ensure menstrual hygiene was easily 
accessible to women/girls in the 
community.
WelNetrutva provided end-to-end 
support through capacity-building 
sessions, guidance in vendor 
selection, exposure visits to 
understand product handling, and 
daily handholding for business 
operations. With a ₹10,000 loan 
from SHG, Mehvish and her 
family launched the enterprise, 
procured pads from a Noida-based 
manufacturer, repacked them into 
six-pad packets at home, and 
distributed them across nearby 
villages. The business soon achieved 
₹20,000 monthly sales, earning a 
monthly profit of ₹6,000-7,000.
Recognising Mehvish’s potential, 
WelNetrutva supported her 
admission into a prestigious 
6-week Entrepreneur Development Workshop organised by the Business 
Department of Aligarh Muslim 
University (AMU), in collaboration 
with the University of Houston, 
United States. With the certification 
programme, Mehvish gained critical 
knowledge of business compliance 
and documentation, registration and 
taxation, marketing strategies, sales 
planning, and financial management.
In the next phase of WelNetrutva, 
Mehvish expanded her operations 
by targeting government and private 
schools in Dibai, Danpur, Anoopshahr, 
Shikarpur at Bulandshahr, and at 
Atrauli in Aligarh. She conducted 
menstrual hygiene workshops and 
ensured availability of sanitary pads 
in the nearby shops. 
 •20 workshops conducted 
 •2,000 adolescent girls reached 
 •Increased awareness and improved 
access across multiple blocks
Today, she runs a flourishing 
enterprise with monthly sales  
of ~₹100,000 and a profit of ₹30,000–
35,000 monthly, and is gradually 
expanding distribution across villages 
and schools. Her work has been 
celebrated by district authorities, and 
she also showcased her products at 
Mahakumbh and UPSRLM exhibitions 
in Agra and Bulandshahr.
Her story is a powerful example of 
what grassroots women can achieve 
when given the right opportunity and 
with their determination. Her journey 
reflects the true spirit of WelNetrutva 
– nurturing women leaders who uplift 
their communities through enterprise 
and empathy. 
Building a better 
life and serving 
Indian Armed 
Forces with pride
Mehvish

1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Purpose, scope, evaluation approach and topline findings
Protiviti conducted the impact assessment for 8 CSR project for FY 2024-25 across WelKrishi, Welspun Super Sports 
Women, WelNetrutva, WelPrakruti, WelShiksha, WelSuraksha, WelSwasthya and WelDisha.

The evaluation was structured around the IRECS framework covering Inclusiveness, Relevance, Effectiveness, Convergence 
and Sustainability. The assessment focussed on the extent to which desired outcomes and impact were achieved; whether 
outputs were effectively and efficiently delivered by implementation teams; identification of risks and opportunities; and 
documentation of success stories and recommendations for future programming.
A qualitative approach was used for drawing inferences on outcome and impact of the project on target beneficiaries. 
The tools included Key Informant’s Interview Questionnaire, Fixed Group Discussion and Observation checklists. In addition 
to the primary beneficiaries covered, other key stakeholders were also interviewed for the purpose of the evaluation.
Thematic area Topline evaluation finding
Education Improved learning outcomes, digital skills, career awareness, classroom participation 
and athlete support.
Healthcare Improved health awareness, access to care, health-seeking behaviour, nutritional 
intake and reduction in out-of-pocket expenditure.
Road Safety Improved awareness, emergency response readiness, Good Samaritan Law 
understanding and healthcare access for drivers.
Livelihood Improved employable skills, income generation, enterprise creation, women’s financial 
decision-making and farm productivity.
Agriculture Improved yield bands, soil health, water-use efficiency, reduction in stalk burning and 
evidence-based advisory through Source Trace.
Environment Expanded green cover, water storage capacity, community ownership and 
environmental awareness.
Women Empowerment Sustained athlete support, medals across levels, international representation, rankings 
and resilient comebacks.
Skill Development Improved job-readiness, confidence, placement-linked training and early income 
generation among placed beneficiaries.The scope of work covered 8 CSR projects for FY 2024-25. The evaluation included intervention beneficiaries and control 
/ non-beneficiaries wherever applicable, along with interviews with other key stakeholders.

IRECS parameter Evaluation focus
Inclusiveness Extent to which the project ensures that all vulnerable stakeholders are equitably benefited 
from all the interventions.
Relevance Extent to which the project interventions are equipped to address the priority needs of the 
targeted stakeholders.
Effectiveness Extent to which the desired project outcomes are achieved by making the best possible use 
of available resources.
Convergence Extent to which the project collaborates with external stakeholders and leverages resources 
for project outputs and outcomes.
Sustainability Extent to which the benefits of the project continues or are likely to continue after the 
project exits.3. EVALUATION FRAMEWORK AND METHODOLOGY

Overview
The global economy grew at around 3.4% in both CY2024 and CY2025, supported by strong technology investments, 
particularly in Artificial Intelligence (AI), as well as supportive policies and stable private-sector activity.  However, the 
environment remained uncertain due to rising trade protectionism and higher US tariffs, which affected global trade. 
Since the beginning of 2026, geopolitical uncertainties and disruptions across global trade routes have contributed to 
volatility in energy and commodity markets. This resulted in higher fuel, raw material and transportation costs, which 
increased input expenses, affected supply chain efficiency and exerted pressure on project execution timelines and 
profitability across various industries.

Our business continued to build momentum during the 
year, supported by disciplined execution and an expanding 
portfolio of projects. The successful completion of the 
Aunta–Simaria Road Project, inaugurated by the Hon'ble 
Prime Minister of India, and our recent Pune–Shirur partially 
elevated road project win reaffirm our capability to win & 
deliver large  scale complex infrastructure.
Our expanding presence across Mumbai's water value 
chain reflects the evolution of our water business into 
an integrated water player. From India's first vertical 
wastewater treatment facility at Dharavi and Asia's largest 
2,000 MLD Water Treatment Facility at Bhandup to the 
Panjrapur WTP, tunnels, pumping stations and rehabilitation 
works, we are present across critical water infrastructure. 
Complementing these capabilities, our technology-led 
waterbody restoration and greywater rejuvenation 
solutions, extends our presence across cities and further 
broadens our national footprint.The recent project wins have strengthened our 
consolidated order book to the highest in our history 
at ~₹20,000 crore (including O&M), providing strong 
revenue visibility. Despite of extended monsoons and 
time intensive approval process, our focus on execution 
and cost discipline enabled a 16% year-on-year growth in 
consolidated EBITDA to ₹845 crore.
Our belief is that successful company is one where 
people grow with the organisation. By building leadership 
capabilities and fostering a high-performance culture, we 
are creating a future-ready organisation. These efforts 
were recognised with WEL being certified as a Great 
Place to Work for the second time, improving our ranking 
by 12 places to 25.
As we enter FY 2027, I am confident that WEL has the 
capabilities, talent and financial strength to lead the next 
phase of infrastructure development, where innovation, 
sustainability and value creation are mutually reinforcing.Outlook
The global economy is expected to face renewed uncertainty 
in CY2026, driven by geopolitical tensions in the Middle 
East and continued volatility in energy and commodity 
markets. These factors may put pressure on inflation, 
financial stability and overall growth. At the same time, the 
rapid adoption of AI is emerging as a key growth driver, 
improving productivity, supporting innovation and creating 
new opportunities across industries, while also reshaping 
workforce requirements and regulatory frameworks. 
Advanced economies are projected to experience a 
gradual slowdown, with growth rates moderating from 
1.9% in CY2025 to 1.8% in CY2026 and then to 1.7% 
in CY2027, reflecting softer consumer demand, tighter 
financial conditions and modest productivity gains.In contrast, emerging markets and developing economies 
are expected to maintain relatively stronger growth, 
although with some volatility. Growth in these economies 
is projected to moderate from 4.4% in CY2025 to 3.9% in 
CY2026, then improve to 4.2% in CY2027 as domestic 
demand and investment gradually recover. Overall, the 
IMF projects global growth to slow to 3.1% in CY2026 and 
improve slightly to 3.2% in CY2027. Inflation is expected 
to increase from 4.1% in CY2025 to 4.4% in CY2026, then 
ease to 3.7% in CY2027. While higher energy costs and 
supply disruptions may affect emerging economies more 
significantly, continued investment in AI and organised 
regulatory support are expected to help sustain global 
economic stability over the medium term.

INDUSTRY OVERVIEWcorridors, and emerging economic clusters, along with 
the growth of Tier-II and Tier-III cities, are improving 
connectivity, enabling economic activity, and creating a 
stronger foundation for sustained infrastructure demand and 
broad-based growth. These developments are expected 
to help businesses expand their reach, deepen customer 
engagement, and adopt technology-driven operating 
models to capture emerging opportunities. Despite global 
uncertainties and input cost pressures, resilient domestic 
demand and evolving consumption patterns are expected 
to support long-term economic growth in India and enable

Source:  https://www.imf.org/-/media/files/publications/weo/2026/
april/english/text.pdf  Overview
India’s economy witnessed strong growth momentum in 
CY2025, with GDP growth accelerating to 7.6%, following 
a robust expansion of 7.1% in CY2024. This growth 
was supported by steady domestic demand, continued 
regulatory reforms and a gradual recovery in both private 
and public investment. The services and industrial sectors 
also contributed positively to economic performance. 
Consumer spending remained resilient throughout the 
year, while investment activity strengthened, particularly 
in the second half, contributing to overall economic 
expansion. 
Despite this progress, the economy faced challenges due 
to global uncertainties. Higher trade tariffs and geopolitical 
tensions affected export performance, particularly in 
West Asia, following developments in late February 2026. 
However, strengthening trade engagement and ongoing 
negotiations with the European Union and the United 
States helped offset some of these pressures and 
reflected improving economic ties. The Government 
of India continued to introduce reforms, including the 
rationalisation of the Goods and Services Tax (GST) and 
the simplification of compliance requirements, thereby 
supporting business confidence and improving the ease 
of doing business. 
Between January and December 2025, the RBI reduced 
the repo rate from 6.5% to 5.25% as inflation eased. 
In April 2026, it kept the rate unchanged at 5.25% and 
moved to a neutral stance to balance growth and inflation.integrated infrastructure systems. These programmes 
have exp anded transport networks, improved logistics 
efficiency and str engthened connectivity in both urban and 
rural areas, while also increasing access to water, housing 
and other basic services.
KEY GOVERNMENT INITIATIVES IN THE 
INFRASTRUCTURE SECTOR
Public capital expenditure remains a key pillar of India’s 
infrastructure-led growth strategy, driving the creation 
of productive assets such as roads, railways, urban 
infrastructure and public utilities. 
India’s budgeted capital expenditure has increased from 
₹2.5 lac crore in FY 2015 to ₹12.2 lac crore in FY 2027, 
representing a ~5x increase over the period, reflecting 
Government’s sustained focus on infrastructure-led growth.
Outlook

Despite global uncertainties, India’s growth is expected to

expected to be supported by continued infrastructure 
development and an improving business environment.

India is home to nearly 18% of the world’s population but 
possesses only about 4% of global freshwater resources, 
creating a widening imbalance between water availability and 
demand. Rapid urbanisation, industrialisation and rising living 
standards are placing increasing pressure on finite water 
resources, while agriculture continues to account for nearly 80% 
of freshwater consumption. As per Niti Aayog’s Composite Water 
Management report. India’s annual per capita water availability 
has declined to around 1,486 cubic metres in 2021 and the 
same is projected to further fall to 1,367 cubic metres by 2031, 
below the internationally recognised water stress threshold 
of 1,700 cubic metres per second. The situation is further 
exacerbated by groundwater depletion, inadequate wastewater 
treatment capacity, pollution of rivers and water bodies, and 
increasing climate variability.WATER SECTOR 
Consequently, water security is no longer solely an 
environmental concern but a strategic infrastructure imperative, 
with significant implications for India’s economic growth, 
urban development and climate resilience. As one of the 
world’s fastest-growing economies, the country’s long-term 
development will increasingly depend on its ability to secure, 
manage and sustainably utilise its water resources. This is driving 
a structural shift from augmenting water supply to creating 
an integrated and circular water ecosystem encompassing 
treatment, transmission, wastewater collection, recycling, reuse 
and climate-resilient infrastructure, creating a multi-decade 
investment opportunity across the entire water value chain.
Key Demand Drivers
India’s water infrastructure investment is supported by several trends expected to sustain demand 
over the long termThis continues to be key focus areas for infrastructure 
development in India supported by increasing water 
demand, urbanisation, industrial growth and the need to 
strengthen long-term water security.
Investments are being directed towards the creation 
and augmentation of storage infrastructure, including 
dams, reservoirs and balancing reservoirs, alongside the 
development of water treatment plants, pumping stations, 
bulk water transmission systems and distribution networks. 
Also, utilities are increasingly undertaking rehabilitation and 
expansion of existing distribution infrastructure to improve 
operational efficiency, reduce non-revenue water and 
ensure reliable water supply.
Government support through AMRUT 2.0 continues to 
drive large-scale investments in urban drinking water 
infrastructure, with the mission targeting universal piped 
water supply across approximately 4,800 statutory towns 
through 2.68 crore new household tap connections while 
reducing non-revenue water to below 20%. Reflecting the 
strong pace of implementation, as of February 2026, 3,528 
water supply projects have been approved across 2,484 
Urban Local Bodies (ULBs), with a cumulative investment 
of approximately ₹1.20 lac crore.
On the rural front, the Government continues to prioritise 
universal access to safe drinking water through Jal Jeevan 
Mission 2.0, which has been extended until December 2028 
with a total outlay of ₹8.69 lac crore. The ₹67,670 crore 
allocation in FY 2026–27 reaffirms the Government’s 
commitment to expanding and strengthening rural drinking 
water infrastructure, while supporting a sustained pipeline 
of water supply projects across the country.India’s urban wastewater sector presents a significant long-
term infrastructure opportunity. Urban centres generate 
over 72,000 MLD of sewage, yet only about 28% is treated, 
underscoring the need for substantial investments in 
sewage treatment plants (STPs), wastewater management 
infrastructure and the modernisation of existing facilities. 
As cities expand sewerage networks and strengthen 
environmental compliance, wastewater treatment is poised 
to become a critical pillar of sustainable urban infrastructure 
development.
Recognising this need, AMRUT 2.0 has made universal 
sewerage and septage management, enhanced wastewater 
treatment capacity, and the promotion of treated wastewater 
reuse central to its objective of creating water-secure and 
sustainable cities. As of Feb 2026, 583 sewerage projects 
have been approved with investments of ₹66,118 crore 
under AMRUT 2.0.
Water recycling is becoming an integral part of India’s urban 
water management strategy, with Tertiary Treated Reverse 
Osmosis (TTRO) playing a pivotal role in enabling circular 
water use. TTRO technology transforms treated sewage 
into industrial-grade water through advanced filtration and 
reverse osmosis, helping conserve freshwater resources 
while ensuring a reliable supply for industrial and commercial 
consumers. As water scarcity intensifies and regulatory 
support for wastewater reuse strengthens, investments in 
TTRO projects are expected to create significant long-term 
opportunities for advanced water infrastructure developers.Water Storage,

Mumbai: Pioneering India’s Circular 
Water Economy
Mumbai’s ongoing wastewater transformation 
represents one of the most significant urban water 
infrastructure initiatives undertaken in India and 
provides a blueprint for the future of water management 
in rapidly urbanising cities. 
The city currently consumes over 4,200 MLD of 
water and generates approximately 3,000 MLD of 
wastewater each day. Historically, limited treatment 
capacity constrained the effective management and 
reuse of this resource. Recognising the strategic 
importance of water security, the Brihanmumbai 
Municipal Corporation (BMC) in 2022 has embarked 
on a comprehensive wastewater transformation 
programme involving the development of seven 
advanced sewage treatment plants with a combined 
treatment capacity of 2,464 MLD and an estimated 
investment of approximately ₹27,000 crore (including 
15 year O&M).
Once completed by 2028, these facilities will 
fundamentally reshape Mumbai’s water ecosystem. 
Nearly 80% of the city’s wastewater will be treated 
through advanced secondary and tertiary processes, 
significantly reducing untreated discharges into rivers, 
creeks and coastal waters. 
More importantly, the programme will transform 
wastewater from an environmental challenge into a valuable economic resource. The new treatment 
infrastructure is expected to generate over 1,200 MLD 
of high-quality tertiary-treated water. This treated 
water can be supplied for industrial operations, power 
generation, construction activities, landscaping and 
municipal applications, reducing dependence on 
freshwater resources and enabling a more efficient 
allocation of water across the city’s needs.
Mumbai’s transformation is emblematic of a 
broader shift taking place across India’s water 
sector. Water management is increasingly viewed 
through the lens of circularity, in which treatment, 
reuse, recycling, resource recovery and lifecycle 
management form an integrated framework for 
sustainable urban development. As cities seek 
to balance economic growth with environmental 
stewardship, wastewater is emerging as a strategic 
asset rather than a by-product to be disposed of.
Welspun Enterprises is proud to contribute to this 
transformation by executing the 418 MLD Dharavi 
Wastewater Treatment Facility, two Water Treatment 
Facilities (2000 MLD at Bhandup and 910 MLD at 
Panjrapur) and a tertiary-treated water conveyance 
tunnel from the Dharavi Facility to Ghatkopar. 
As Mumbai advances towards a circular water 
economy, these assets will play an important role 
in improving water reuse, strengthening urban 
resilience and supporting the city’s long-term 
sustainability objectives.Rural Wastewater Management under Swachh 
Bharat Mission (Grameen)
The rapid expansion of rural piped water supply under the 
Jal Jeevan Mission has brought wastewater management 
into sharp focus as the next critical infrastructure priority. 
As the volume of household greywater continues to 
rise, investments in collection, treatment and reuse 
infrastructure are becoming essential to safeguard water 
resources, improve sanitation and sustain the benefits of 
rural water supply programmes.
Recognising the growing need for rural wastewater 
management, the Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) Phase 
II has expanded its focus beyond sanitation to include 
comprehensive solid and liquid waste management. 
The programme envisages an outlay of approximately 
₹1.40 lac crore, over FY 21-26, and as per the reports, 
Phase III is under development. The mission is accelerating 
the development of village-level greywater collection, 
treatment and reuse infrastructure, fostering sustainable 
water resource management across rural India.

Bharatmala Pariyojna
Bharatmala Pariyojana was the flagship highway development programme of the Government of India. Approved in 2017 
with an estimated outlay of ₹5.35 lac crore, the programme aims to develop 34,800 km of National Highway corridors, 
including economic corridors, feeder routes, border roads, coastal roads, port connectivity roads, and expressways. As of 
March 2026, projects covering 26,425 km had been awarded, while around 22,590 km had already been constructed. 
The programme has played a significant role in improving freight movement, reducing logistics costs, and strengthening 
connectivity to remote and strategic regions of the country. 
source: PIB – Bharatmala Pariyojana: A Vision for Integrated National Connectivity (June 2026)
While roads and highways remain a key infrastructure priority, 
sustained investments across railways, metro systems, 
airports, ports and multimodal logistics are reshaping 
India’s transportation landscape. The Government’s focus 
on creating integrated transport networks is expected 
to improve connectivity, enhance freight movement and 
reduce logistics costs, thereby supporting economic 
growth. As infrastructure development increasingly adopts 
a multimodal approach, opportunities are expanding for 
companies with strong engineering expertise, complex 
project execution capabilities and disciplined capital 
allocation.
Metro Rail
Metro rail has emerged as one of India’s fastest-growing 
urban infrastructure segments, driven by rapid

transportation. India’s operational metro network expanded 
from 248 km across five cities in 2014 to over 1,095 km 
across 26 cities by 2025, making it one of the largest 
metro systems globally. Government support has remained 
robust, with annual budgetary allocation for metro rail 
increasing from ₹5,798 crore in FY14 to ₹29,550 crore 
in FY26. The continued expansion of metro corridors is 
expected to improve urban mobility, reduce congestion, 
lower emissions and support inclusive economic growth.
